title: Segal spaces, strict mapping fibres and completeness
statement:
Use the small simplicial sets and realization-based weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the Kan fibrations of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and Reedy matching maps of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A simplicial space is a functor $W:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$; its first coordinate is the outer degree, and write $W_n$ for the simplicial set in the second coordinate. Let $e_W=(d_1,d_0):W_1\to W_0\times W_0$, and define $M_W(x,y)=W_1\times_{W_0\times W_0}\{(x,y)\}$ for vertices $x,y$ of $W_0$. A map $f:W\to V$ induces the strict-pullback map $M_W(x,y)\to M_V(fx,fy)$. Let $P_n(W)$ be the simplicial set with inner $q$-simplices strings of $n$ consecutive outer edges of $W_{\bullet,q}$, with their $n+1$ vertices and equality of matched endpoints. Restriction to the consecutive edges defines $W_n\to P_n(W)$. Say $W$ is Reedy fibrant if each outer matching map $W_n\to M_nW$ is a Kan fibration, using the nonidentity opposite-injective maps for the matching diagram. Say $W$ is Segal if it is Reedy fibrant and each consecutive-edge map is a weak homotopy equivalence for $n\geq2$.

Two outer edges with fixed source $x$ and target $y$ have the same mapping component if their lifts to the strict fibre $M_W(x,y)$ have equal classes in $\pi_0M_W(x,y)$. An outer edge $a:x\to y$ is an equivalence arrow if it has an inverse edge $g:y\to x$ and outer $2$-simplices with consecutive edges $(a,g)$ and $(g,a)$, respectively, whose long edges have the same mapping components as $s_0x$ and $s_0y$. For Segal $W$ these are exactly the arrows invertible in its homotopy category, whose morphisms are the mapping-fibre components and whose composition is given by the degree-two Segal map and $d_1$. Define $W_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq W_1$ to be the union of components containing equivalence arrows: an inner simplex belongs precisely when all its vertices are in such components. Say $W$ is complete if it is Segal and the actual degeneracy $s_0:W_0\to W_1$ factors through $W_{\mathrm{eq}}$ by a weak homotopy equivalence. A map $f:W\to V$ is essentially surjective if every vertex $z$ of $V_0$ is the target of an equivalence arrow whose source is $fx$ for some vertex $x$ of $W_0$.

source.place: Rezk, A model for the homotopy theory of homotopy theory, Sections 2.3-2.4, 4.1, 5.1, 5.3, 5.5, 5.7-5.8, 6 and 7.4; the strict mapping fibres, inverse equations in their components, and identity degeneracy are the conventions used by Section 14.
